correctness.rationale: The exact identity \(\log D(m^2)=\log(3/2)\omega(m)+H(m)\) follows from prime-power factors, with \(m=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\). For square cutoffs, \(m\) has weight \((2m-1)/T^2\), and the conditional square gap is an equispaced grid. For each finite prime set weighted CRT gives independent geometric valuations; the uniform tail bound \(2\sum_{p>B}1/(p(p-1))\to0\) establishes convergence and finite a.s. support of the Euler correction. A moment-based Erdős–Kac argument in each fixed residue class, followed by finite-valution conditioning and weighted partial summation, proves joint independence of the Gaussian and correction coordinates. The exact grid bound gives the independent uniform phase. Removing at most \(2T+1\) integers handles arbitrary cutoffs; Slutsky handles the correction in the Gaussian normalization. The Euler product and two precise atoms are reconstructed algebraically; the embedded standard-library verifier independently checks all finite arithmetic ranges and does not purport to prove weak convergence.

originality.rationale: The originating article arXiv:2602.20808v1 defines the same square-shifted divisor ratio and studies an asymptotic for its sum (Theorem 2.1), not the joint three-coordinate law. Levy–Squillace Theorem 2 proves a scalar Gaussian limit for prime counts under perturbed measures, and Tenenbaum–Verwee Theorem 1.1 an atomic additive marginal distribution. Tenenbaum–Verwee Theorem 1.3 treats strongly additive functions whose limit laws are continuous, whereas the correction here vanishes at primes and is positive at prime squares and has atoms; it therefore does not directly imply the stated conditional independence. Targeted published-record and primary-literature searches found no equivalent statement. Residual risk remains for an unindexed stronger joint additive theorem or an extension of the conditional Erdős–Wintner method; published special marginal cases are not claimed as novel.
residual_risks: Generic unindexed joint limit theorems for additive functions with Gaussian divergent and atomic bounded components could subsume the first two coordinates.

Tenenbaum–Verwee explicitly note that a completely general conditional theorem could be obtained by their method, but the published Theorem 1.3 is restricted to a strongly additive function with continuous distribution.
The accessible excerpt of Dixit–Murty is not a complete full-text inspection; its subject is locally truncated prime counts rather than the exact shift.
Search results cannot prove global mathematical uniqueness; independent priority review remains necessary.

value.rationale: The object is the natural square-completion divisor statistic of Mihoub. Its mean does not determine typical fluctuations or the distribution of its intrinsic correction. The complete product limit resolves the coexistence and independence of Gaussian bulk prime-count variation, an arithmetically discrete squarefull-prime correction, and a uniform geometric within-block phase. Its exact first two atom masses give reproducible positive-frequency structural predictions, including a nontrivial first positive atom. This is a motivated full limiting classification of three genuinely different statistics, not merely a renamed scalar Erdős–Kac theorem, an arbitrary restricted parameter, or a finite numerical observation. The result does not claim a new generic Erdős–Kac or Erdős–Wintner theorem.
